directAnswer: You can disable startup apps in Windows by using the Task Manager or the Settings app, depending on your version of Windows.
summary: Disabling startup applications can help improve boot times and system performance.

sections.heading: Using Task Manager
sections.body: You can easily manage startup applications through the Task Manager. This method is available in Windows 10 and Windows 11.

sections.heading: Using Settings App
sections.body: In Windows 10 and Windows 11, you can also disable startup apps via the Settings app for a more user-friendly approach.

steps.title: Open Task Manager
steps.detail: Right-click the taskbar and select 'Task Manager' or press Ctrl + Shift + Esc.

steps.title: Go to Startup Tab
steps.detail: In Task Manager, click on the 'Startup' tab to see a list of applications that run at startup.

steps.title: Disable Applications
steps.detail: Select the application you want to disable and click the 'Disable' button in the bottom right corner.

steps.title: Using Settings App
steps.detail: Open Settings (Windows + I), navigate to 'Apps' > 'Startup', and toggle off the apps you want to disable.

faqs.question: Will disabling startup apps improve my computer's performance?
faqs.answer: Yes, disabling unnecessary startup apps can lead to faster boot times and improved overall performance.

faqs.question: Can I re-enable a disabled startup app later?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can re-enable any disabled startup app by following the same steps and selecting 'Enable' instead.

faqs.question: Are there any apps I should not disable?
faqs.answer: Be cautious when disabling apps related to system processes or security software, as this may affect system functionality.

caveats: Disabling certain startup applications may affect the functionality of specific programs or services.
